## Natural history notes

A native deciduous tree characterized by simple glossy leaves, dark bluish-black fruits, and a swollen or buttressed trunk base in frequently flooded sites. Swamp Tupelo occurs throughout Florida in cypress swamps, wet flatwoods, pond margins, sloughs, floodplains, and other low-lying areas that remain saturated or inundated for extended periods. It is especially adapted to acidic, poorly drained organic or clay soils and can tolerate seasonal flooding better than the closely related Black Tupelo. Its flowers provide resources for pollinators, while the fleshy fruits are eaten and dispersed by birds and other wildlife, making it an important component of southeastern swamp forests.
